# Microbial Metallomics

> Microbial metallomics is the integrated study of the metals and metalloids a microbe uses, stores, senses, and competes for. This site is an independent, comprehensively cited field guide: the science, the metals, the methods, the microbiome/health connections, applications, the research landscape, a who's who, an in-depth glossary, a research library of paper reviews, original research, and a blog developing the metal–microbiome–disease axis.

Core thesis (the metal–microbiome–disease axis): heavy-metal exposure reshapes the gut microbiome, and microbiome disruption drives disease — so heavy-metal exposure can drive disease through this microbiome-mediated mechanistic pathway. See /blog/metal-microbiome-disease-axis.

## Key concepts (each has a dedicated page under /glossary/)
- [Calprotectin](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/calprotectin): Calprotectin is an abundant neutrophil protein complex (an S100A8/S100A9 heterodimer) that helps defend the host by sequestering manganese and zinc from microbes, and is measured in stool as a biomarker of gut inflammation.
- [Dissimilatory Metal Reduction](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/dissimilatory-metal-reduction): Dissimilatory metal reduction is a form of anaerobic microbial respiration in which cells conserve energy by transferring respiratory electrons onto an oxidized metal, such as Fe(III), Mn(IV), or U(VI), used as the terminal electron acceptor.
- [Irving–Williams Series](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/irving-williams-series): The Irving–Williams series is the empirical order of thermodynamic stability for high-spin divalent first-row transition-metal complexes, Mn(II) < Fe(II) < Co(II) < Ni(II) < Cu(II) > Zn(II), which holds regardless of the ligand.
- [Metal Intoxication](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metal-intoxication): Metal intoxication is the offensive arm of nutritional immunity in which host immune cells flood a trapped microbe with toxic excess copper and zinc to mismetalate its enzymes and destroy iron-sulfur clusters.
- [Metal Sparing](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metal-sparing): Metal sparing is the remodeling of a microbe's proteome during metal starvation, in which metal-requiring proteins are replaced by isozymes that use a different metal or no metal at all, thereby reducing cellular demand for the scarce element.
- [Metallochaperone](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metallochaperone): A metallochaperone is a soluble intracellular carrier protein that binds a specific metal ion and delivers it by direct protein-protein contact to a designated target enzyme or transporter.
- [Metallome](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metallome): The metallome is the entirety of metal and metalloid species within a cell or organism, comprising free ions together with all metal- and metalloid-containing biomolecules.
- [Metallomics](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metallomics): Metallomics is the integrated study of the metallome — the identity, quantity, distribution, coordination chemistry and biological function of all metals and metalloids in a cell, tissue or organism.
- [Metallophore](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metallophore): A metallophore is a low-molecular-weight molecule secreted by microorganisms to bind and acquire a specific scarce metal ion from the environment or host.
- [Metalloproteome](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metalloproteome): The metalloproteome is the complete set of metal-binding proteins in an organism or cell, encompassing every protein that requires a metal ion or metal cofactor for its structure or function.
- [Metalloregulation](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metalloregulation): Metalloregulation is the process by which cells sense intracellular metal-ion concentrations through metal-responsive regulatory proteins that switch target genes on or off to maintain metal homeostasis.
- [Metallostasis](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/metallostasis): Metallostasis is the coordinated sensing, buffering, trafficking, and sparing of metal ions that keeps each essential metal's bioavailability within a narrow physiological range inside a cell.
- [Mismetallation](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/mismetallation): Mismetallation is the binding of a metalloprotein's metal site by the wrong metal ion — usually a more competitive one — which inactivates or misdirects the enzyme.
- [Nutritional Immunity](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/nutritional-immunity): Nutritional immunity is the host defense strategy of controlling transition-metal availability—withholding iron, zinc, and manganese or intoxicating microbes with copper and zinc—to limit the growth of invading pathogens.
- [Siderophore](https://microbialmetallomics.com/glossary/siderophore): A siderophore is a small, high-affinity iron(III)-chelating molecule that microbes secrete to scavenge scarce environmental iron and import it into the cell.

## Original research (Zenodo, by Karen Pendergrass / Paleo Foundation)
- [Six Decades of Fertilizer Use Built a Legacy of Cadmium, Nickel, and Lead in Soils and Diets](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/heavy-metals-in-fertilizers-contamination-trends): A food metallomics review (1960–2025) showing how phosphate and urea fertilizers loaded soils, crops, and diets with cadmium, nickel, lead, and chromium.
- [Heavy Metals and Microbial Metallomics: A New Framework for the US Obesity Epidemic](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/heavy-metals-microbial-metallomics-obesity-epidemic): How dietary cadmium, arsenic, lead, and nickel may disrupt gut microbial metallomics—driving dysbiosis, inflammation, and insulin resistance behind obesity.
- [Developmental Readiness Is Not Toxicokinetic Safety: Heavy Metals in Vegetable-Based Baby Foods](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/metal-vulnerability-vegetable-baby-foods): Developmental readiness for solids does not ensure toxicokinetic safety: leafy greens, brassicas and root crops concentrate lead, cadmium and arsenic in baby foods.
- [Concentration-Based Heavy Metal Standards to Reduce Real Exposure in Infant and Child Foods](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/hmtc-infant-child-food-standards-2026): HMTc 2026 sets concentration-based, as-sold action levels for lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury, nickel and other heavy metals in infant and child foods.
- [Nickel as a Catalytic Driver of Necrotizing Enterocolitis](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/nickel-necrotizing-enterocolitis): Dietary nickel in infant formula may activate nickel-dependent microbial enzymes (urease, glyoxalase I) that drive necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm infants.
- [A Unified Model for FIP-Associated Gingivitis in Cats: Disrupting Microbial Shielding and Restoring Nutritional Immunity](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/lactoferrin-itraconazole-fip-gingivitis-cats): How itraconazole and lactoferrin may treat FIP-linked gingivitis in cats by disrupting polymicrobial biofilms and restoring metal-based nutritional immunity.
- [Microbiome Medicine Journal: Restoring Causal Structure to Disease Through Microbial Metallomics](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/microbiome-medicine-journal-volume-1): Microbiome Medicine Journal Vol. I sets out a mechanism-first framework linking microbial ecology, host metallome regulation, and metal dyshomeostasis to disease.
- [From Dysbiosis to Dyshomeostasis: Reframing Parkinson's Through a Metallomic–Microbiome Lens](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/parkinsons-dysbiosis-to-dyshomeostasis): A metallomics framework reframes Parkinson's as metal dyshomeostasis: iron, manganese, copper, zinc and nickel dysregulation drives dysbiosis and neuron loss.
- [The MC1R–Parkinson's Link May Be a Metallomic Story, Not a Cosmetic One](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/melanin-metal-parkinsons-redheads): A hypothesis linking MC1R red-hair variants to Parkinson's risk via melanin-metal chemistry: how copper, zinc, and iron shape neuromelanin's redox buffering.
- [Parkinson's Disease as a Disorder of Metal Dyshomeostasis Amplified by Microbial Ecology](https://microbialmetallomics.com/research/microbial-metallomics-parkinsons-framework): A synthesis framework proposing Parkinson's disease begins with heavy-metal dyshomeostasis that drives ferroptosis, gut dysbiosis, and α-synuclein pathology.

## Blog — the metal–microbiome–disease axis
- [Tampon Metals and the Vaginal Microbiome: The Blind Spot in the Risk Assessment](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/tampon-metals-vaginal-microbiome-blind-spot): A toxicological risk assessment found tampon metals pose negligible systemic risk. But bioavailable there means absorbed into the blood, and the vaginal microbial community on the tampon surface was never assessed.
- [The Metal-Microbiome-Disease Axis: How Heavy Metals May Drive Disease Through the Gut](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/metal-microbiome-disease-axis): Heavy-metal exposure reshapes the gut microbiome, and a disrupted microbiome drives disease. Chain those two well-evidenced links together and you get a mechanistic hypothesis: metals can cause disease through the microbiome. Here is the whole case, link by link, with the strength of the evidence named at each step.
- [Arsenic and the Gut Microbiome: A Two-Way Street](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/arsenic-gut-microbiome-two-way): Inorganic arsenic remodels the gut community, and the community in turn governs how much arsenic your body absorbs, transforms, and excretes. The evidence for this bidirectional loop is strong in animals and suggestive in humans.
- [Cadmium and the Gut Microbiome: A Hidden Route to Metabolic Disease](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/cadmium-gut-microbiome-metabolic-disease): A growing body of animal and human evidence suggests cadmium does not just poison cells directly. It reshapes the gut microbiome, breaches the intestinal barrier, and feeds the metabolic dysfunction that ends in fatty liver and diabetes.
- [Feeding the Enemy: How Dietary Iron Reshapes the Gut Microbiome and Raises Enteric Infection Risk](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/dietary-iron-microbiome-enteric-infection): Most oral iron is never absorbed. It reaches the colon, where it favors enteropathogens over protective bacteria. Randomized trials in African infants show iron fortification remodels the microbiome, inflames the gut, and raises diarrhea risk.
- [Does Lead Harm the Developing Brain Through the Gut Microbiome?](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/lead-gut-microbiome-neurodevelopment): Lead reshapes the gut microbiome in animals and children, and a growing body of work asks whether that dysbiosis is a hidden channel through which lead injures the developing brain.
- [Mercury, Methylmercury, and the Microbiome: How Gut Microbes Shape Neurotoxic Risk](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/mercury-methylmercury-microbiome): Gut bacteria are active mercury chemists: they demethylate methylmercury and speed its excretion, mercury exposure reshapes the microbiome, and that feedback loop helps set an individual's neurotoxic risk.
- [How Low-Dose Heavy Metals May Reshape the Gut Microbiome to Drive Obesity](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/metals-microbiome-obesity-metabolic-syndrome): A growing body of animal, mechanistic, and human evidence supports the hypothesis that chronic low-dose metal exposure is an upstream, microbiome-mediated contributor to obesity and metabolic syndrome.
- [Metals, the Microbiome, and Parkinson's: A Gut-First Pathway to Neurodegeneration](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/metals-microbiome-parkinsons-neurodegeneration): Manganese, iron, and lead are epidemiologically tied to Parkinson's, and the gut microbiome may be the missing intermediary. Here is the evidence for a metal-microbiome-disease pathway to neurodegeneration.
- [How Dietary Nickel Arms Gut Bacteria — and May Fuel Gut Disease](https://microbialmetallomics.com/blog/nickel-gut-microbiome-disease): Nickel is not just a nutrient — it is the cofactor that switches on urease and [NiFe]-hydrogenase in gut Enterobacteriaceae. Here is the evidence linking dietary nickel to necrotizing enterocolitis and IBD, and the gaps that remain.

## Paper reviews (research library)
- [Iron Fortification and the Kenyan Infant Gut Microbiome](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/iron-fortification-kenyan-infant-microbiome): A full review of Jaeggi et al. (Gut 2015): iron-fortified porridge increased pathogenic E. coli and enterobacteria, cut bifidobacteria, and inflamed the gut in Kenyan infants.
- [Childhood Blood Metals and the Gut Microbiome: Evidence from the GESTE Cohort](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/childhood-blood-metals-microbiome-geste): GESTE cohort links childhood blood metals (Mn, Se, Cd, Hg, Pb) to gut microbiome composition in 6-7 year olds; manganese and selenium tied to bacterial phyla.
- [A Multi-Omics + MR Enterography Model for Predicting Bowel Damage in Crohn's Disease](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/crohns-multiomics-mre-bowel-damage): Two-center study fusing gut microbiome, fecal and serum metabolomics, and MR enterography into a model predicting cumulative Crohn's bowel damage (AUC 0.857).
- [Gut Microbiome and Childhood Stunting in Low- and Middle-Income Countries](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/gut-microbiome-childhood-stunting-lmic): Systematic review of 14 studies links childhood stunting in LMICs to inflammatory gut pathobionts and depleted butyrate producers, driving impaired linear growth.
- [HERFD-XAS: High-Resolution X-ray Speciation of Biological Metals](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/herfd-xas-metallomics): HERFD-XAS sharpens X-ray absorption spectra by rejecting core-hole broadening, resolving mercury, selenium, and arsenic speciation in dilute biological samples for metallomics.
- [Iron Fortification, the Infant Gut Microbiome, and Diarrhea Risk](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/iron-fortification-infant-microbiome-diarrhea): Iron fortification shifts the infant gut microbiome toward enterobacteria and pathogenic E. coli, cutting protective bifidobacteria and raising diarrhea risk.
- [Iron Supplements and the Gut Microbiome in Reproductive-Age Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/iron-supplements-microbiome-reproductive-women): A 21-day randomized placebo-controlled trial found ferrous fumarate did not significantly alter fecal microbiome composition in Australian reproductive-age women.
- [Iron- and Zinc-Biofortified Foods and the Gut Microbiota](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/iron-zinc-biofortified-foods-gut-microbiota): Systematic review of iron/zinc-biofortified bean and wheat diets in the Gallus gallus model: staples raised SCFA-producing Lactobacillus and cut enteric pathogens.
- [Lactobacillus plantarum 299v and Oral Iron Therapy Tolerance](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/lactobacillus-plantarum-299v-oral-iron): A randomized trial shows the probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum 299v reduces oral iron side effects and improves iron status in iron-deficiency anemia patients.
- [Lactoferrin vs. Ferrous Sulfate Through a Metallomics Lens](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/lactoferrin-vs-ferrous-sulfate): Meta-analyses show oral lactoferrin can match or outperform ferrous sulfate for iron repletion, lowering IL-6 and hepcidin with fewer gut side effects.
- [Intestinal Biomarkers and the Non-Motor Phenotype of Parkinson's Disease](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/parkinsons-intestinal-biomarkers-nonmotor): Parkinson's patients with constipation show higher fecal calprotectin, reduced SCFAs, lower gut diversity, and greater IBD genetic risk, linking gut inflammation to non-motor severity.
- [Pediatric Gut Microbiome Composition in Health: What a Systematic Review Reveals](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/pediatric-gut-microbiome-health-review): A systematic review of 42 studies finds geography, diet, and 16S sequencing method, not age, shape healthy children's Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes gut profiles.
- [Perinatal Tobacco Exposure Reshapes the Child Gut Microbiota](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/perinatal-tobacco-child-gut-microbiota): A Spanish birth-cohort study found prenatal tobacco smoke, a source of cadmium and lead, lowers gut Akkermansia and raises Dorea in children by age 7.
- [Prenatal Acetaminophen, the Infant Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Cognition](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/prenatal-acetaminophen-microbiome-cognition): GESTE cohort links prenatal acetaminophen and caffeine to childhood gut microbiome shifts and cognition; Proteobacteria abundance modified WISC-IV scores.
- [Prenatal Metal Exposure, the Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Intestinal Inflammation](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/prenatal-metals-microbiome-child-inflammation): A 2024 PROGRESS cohort study links prenatal copper and cesium exposure, interacting with specific gut microbes, to elevated fecal calprotectin in children.
- [Arsenic Exposure Reshapes the Gut Microbiome of Bangladeshi Children, Enriching Resistance-Carrying E. coli](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/arsenic-gut-ecoli-children-bangladesh): Arsenic-exposed Bangladeshi children carry more gut Proteobacteria and E. coli bearing arsenic-resistance (ars) and antibiotic-resistance-like genes, a metal-microbiome case study.
- [Copper in Infectious Disease: Both Sides of the Penny](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/copper-infectious-disease-both-sides): How the immune system weaponizes copper against pathogens: macrophage copper bursts, phagosomal intoxication, fungal copper detox, and copper nutritional immunity.
- [Gallium as an Iron Mimic: Disrupting Pseudomonas Iron Metabolism in Cystic Fibrosis](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/gallium-cystic-fibrosis-pseudomonas): Gallium substitutes for iron to sabotage Pseudomonas aeruginosa iron metabolism. A Phase 1 CF trial (Goss et al., Sci Transl Med 2018) found IV gallium improved lung function.
- [The Human Microbiome Across Body Sites: Gut, Skin, Oral, Vaginal and Lung](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/heavy-metals-gut-microbiota-review): How the human microbiome differs across the gut, skin, oral, vaginal and lung niches, how it is acquired and disrupted, and why heavy-metal exposure matters.
- [Heavy Metals and the Gut Microbiota: A Systematic Review](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/heavy-metals-gut-microbiota-systematic-review): Systematic review of 12 human studies links arsenic, lead, mercury, and cadmium exposure to gut microbiota dysbiosis, leaky gut, and disease, with dietary mitigation.
- [Iron Chelation Therapy in Transfusion-Dependent Thalassemia](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/iron-chelation-therapy-thalassemia): Clinical review of deferoxamine, deferiprone, and deferasirox for transfusion iron overload in thalassemia, covering cardiac and hepatic iron outcomes measured by MRI T2*.
- [Metal Availability and Immune Function During Infection](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/metal-availability-immune-function-infection): How zinc, iron, manganese, and copper availability shapes neutrophil and macrophage function during infection through nutritional immunity, calprotectin, and phagosomal metal handling.
- [Nutritional Immunity and Trace Metals in Infection](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/nutritional-immunity-trace-metals-infection): How the host uses iron, zinc, manganese and copper handling as nutritional immunity to starve or poison pathogens, plus metal-based therapeutic strategies.
- [Prebiotics Blunt the Gut Cost of Iron-Fortified Cereal in Kenyan Infants](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/prebiotic-iron-cereal-kenyan-infants): In a Kenyan infant RCT, adding prebiotic GOS/FOS to iron-fortified cereal raised iron absorption 60% and reduced gut inflammation, pathogens, and dysbiosis.
- [Prenatal Lead Exposure and the Childhood Gut Microbiome](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/prenatal-lead-childhood-gut-microbiome): Prenatal lead exposure is negatively linked to the childhood gut microbiome: metagenomics from a Mexico City cohort ties maternal Pb to fewer beneficial bacteria.
- [Prenatal Metal Exposure, the Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Depression](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/prenatal-metals-microbiome-childhood-depression): A Mexico City birth-cohort study links a prenatal zinc-cobalt profile plus specific gut bacteria to 15.4% higher childhood depression scores at ages 9-11.
- [Spatial Metallomics in Colorectal Cancer: Copper-Immune and Iron-EMT Pathways](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/spatial-metallomics-colorectal-cancer): Spatial metallomics pairs LA-ICP-TOF-MS with Visium transcriptomics in colorectal cancer, mapping copper to immune genes and iron to EMT at the tumor front.
- [Proteome-Scale Mapping of Iron-Binding Proteins in Bread Wheat](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/wheat-iron-binding-proteome): A proteome-wide scan of bread wheat mapped ~600 iron-binding proteins with Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites coordinated by His, Glu, Asp and Cys, aiding metallomics.
- [Nitric Oxide Sensing by the [4Fe-4S] Regulator ArnR](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/arnr-4fe4s-nitric-oxide-sensing): ArnR uses a [4Fe-4S] cluster to sense nitric oxide: NO nitrosylates the cluster, abolishing DNA binding and derepressing nitrate-respiration and hmp genes.
- [Maternal Metallomic Profiles in Pregnancy with Obesity: A Secondary Analysis of UPBEAT](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/heavy-metals-obesity-pregnancy-upbeat): UPBEAT analysis profiled 18 serum metals in 755 pregnant women with obesity: elevated manganese linked to antepartum haemorrhage, phosphorus to NICU care.
- [The Iron Metalloproteome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Under Oxic and Anoxic Conditions](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/iron-metalloproteome-pseudomonas): Native metalloproteomics maps how Pseudomonas aeruginosa partitions iron across four protein complexes, with denitrification raising iron demand in anoxia.
- [Iron-Sulfur Clusters and Oxygen in Human Disease](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/iron-sulfur-clusters-oxygen-disease): How iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster biogenesis and oxygen shape human disease: NFS1 in lung cancer, hyperoxia injury, and hypoxia therapy for Friedreich ataxia.
- [[NiFe]-Hydrogenase Cofactor Biosynthesis and the Hyp Maturation Proteins (HypA-F) in E. coli](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/nife-cofactor-biosynthesis-ecoli): How E. coli builds the NiFe(CN)2CO cofactor of [NiFe]-hydrogenases: the HypA-F maturation proteins, cyanide and CO ligand synthesis, and nickel insertion.
- [The Zinc Clasp: How Zn2+ Shapes T-Cell Signaling](https://microbialmetallomics.com/library/zinc-clasp-cd4-cd8-lck-tcell): The zinc clasp is a Zn2+-bridged interface that tethers the kinase Lck to CD4 and CD8 coreceptors, a labile-zinc switch central to T-cell activation and immunity.
